Then, calculate the discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac. If D > 0, there are two real roots; if D = 0, one real root; and if D < 0, the roots are complex. Use the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √D) / (2a) to find the solutions. Always check the results by substituting back into the original equation.

To find the stationary points of y=f(x), first compute the derivative f'(x) to determine the slope. Set f'(x)=0 and solve for x to find the candidate points. Next, check the second derivative f''(x) at these points to determine if they are minima, maxima, or points of inflection. Finally, plug the x-values back into f(x) to get the corresponding y-values, thereby locating the stationary points.
